citation: Allen, J. P., Hafen, C. A., Gregory, A. C., Mikami, A. Y., & Pianta, R. (2015). Enhancing Secondary School Instruction and Student Achievement: Replication and Extension of the My Teaching Partner-Secondary Intervention. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 8(4), 475-489. https://doi.org/10.1080/19345747.2015.1017680
design: Teacher/Class-level RCT (single TPD arm: My Teaching Partner-Secondary [MTP-S] web-mediated coaching vs. business-as-usual in-service training). 86 secondary-school teachers from 5 schools randomly assigned (44 MTP-S / 42 control after attrition; recruited 97), stratified within school x grade-level x content area; ~1,194 students (659 intervention, 536 control). Two-year intervention; outcomes at end of Year 2. Subject = mixed core academic subjects (math/science and English/social studies); grade = mixed (11% middle school, 89% high school). Impacts via HLM (students within teachers within schools; school level dropped after preliminary analyses found no significant school effects), covarying student prior-year SOL score plus demographics.
problems: Original publisher/PMC PDF could not be saved directly: the legal OA copy is the NIH author manuscript on PubMed Central (PMC5323067 / nihms847421.pdf), but PMC serves it behind a JavaScript proof-of-work download challenge that blocks scripted (curl/WebFetch) download, and the article is NOT in the PMC Open-Access bulk subset (PMC OA service returns 'idIsNotOpenAccess'; EuropePMC render endpoints also fail; Unpaywall lists it as green-OA submittedVersion at PMC with no direct url_for_pdf). Full text was instead obtained legally and in full via NCBI's BioC RESTful API for the same PMC manuscript (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/bionlp/RESTful/pmcoa.cgi/BioC_json/PMC5323067/unicode), which includes Table 1, Table 2, and all results text. data/fulltext/allen_2015.pdf is a 7-page PDF re-rendered from that legally-obtained author-manuscript text (with a provenance banner on page 1); it is NOT the Taylor & Francis typeset PDF, which is paywalled. -- Substantive extraction notes: (1) The report gives a SINGLE pooled student-achievement effect across all content areas; it explicitly tested content area (English/history/SS vs. math/science) as a moderator and found NO main or moderating effect (p > .50), so it does NOT report separate Reading vs. STEM effect sizes. The one extracted g therefore spans both Reading and STEM subjects and is mapped to outcome_subject='Other' (mixed/pooled composite). (2) Two g values are reported for the SAME contrast: g=.31 simple (unadjusted) and g=.48 covariate-adjusted (prior-year achievement + demographics). Per spec the pretest/covariate-adjusted estimate (g=.48) is extracted as the primary value; the .31 is noted. (3) The standardizing SD is not stated explicitly; the reported adjusted g=.48 with HLM impact b=14.67 implies a standardizing SD of ~30.56 SOL points (residual/within-group posttest SD), so the impact SE (5.39) yields g_se ~ .176, g_var ~ .031. These derived variance figures are approximate (back-computed), so the SE/var are best-effort, not paper-stated.

effect_sizes.arm_label: My Teaching Partner-Secondary (MTP-S) web-mediated coaching vs. business-as-usual in-service professional development (single TPD arm)
effect_sizes.test_name: Virginia Standards of Learning (SOL) end-of-course standardized state achievement test, pooled across teachers' focal core courses (math/science and English/social studies); scaled 200-600
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of Year 2 of the 2-year intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Hedges' g = 0.48 taken directly from the report (Results text, p.481/offset 26159): the covariate-adjusted standardized mean difference favoring MTP-S, derived from the HLM impact (Table 2: MTP-S intervention coefficient B = 14.67**, SE = 5.39, p<.01) standardizing by the within-group/residual SOL SD (~30.56 points, implied by b/g = 14.67/0.48). Positive = favors TPD. Small-sample correction J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1193 gives J = 0.9994, negligible, so g_reported already = g. g_se = J*(SE_b/s) = 0.9994*(5.39/30.56) = 0.176; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.0311 (back-computed; not paper-stated).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Results 'Primary Intervention Effects' p.481 (BioC offset 26159) for g=.48/.31; Table 2 (p.482) MTP-S coefficient B=14.67**, SE=5.39; Table 1 (p.482) sample sizes; Figure 1 (means by group).
effect_sizes.notes: Single pooled student-achievement contrast (one TPD arm vs. business-as-usual). The report's HEADLINE/confirmatory result is the covariate-adjusted Hedges' g = 0.48 (after covarying individual prior-year SOL score [r=.77 with outcome], grade level, family poverty, racial/ethnic minority status); the SIMPLE unadjusted comparison gave Hedges' g = 0.31 (same contrast, no covariates) -- not extracted as a separate row since it is the same contrast; per spec the covariate-adjusted estimate is preferred. Effect was equivalent to moving the typical student from the 50th to the 59th percentile. Content area (English/history/SS vs. math/science) tested as moderator: NO main or moderating effect (p>.50) -> single pooled effect across subjects, hence outcome_subject='Other'. Clustering: design randomized teachers/classrooms (86 clusters); HLM nested students-within-teachers-within-schools, but preliminary 3-level models found no significant school effects (all p>.35) so the school level was dropped; the teacher/class HLM impact estimate accounts for the relevant nesting -> cluster_adjusted=true. ICC not reported as a single design-effect value (left null per spec; never guess). n_t=659, n_c=536 from Table 1 (male+female counts); paper text rounds total to 1,194 (Table 1 sums to 1,195). Tests are Virginia state SOL end-of-course exams (standardized, independent of developers). Conflict-of-interest note: R. Pianta co-owns the MTP dissemination company.
